title: Correct initial flux
description: Essential: Student states the magnetic flux through the plane is Φ₁ = B·S.

title: Correct flux after rotation
description: Essential: Student calculates the flux after a 60° rotation as Φ₂ = B·S·cos(60°) = (1/2)BS.

title: Correct flux change
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the change in flux as ΔΦ = Φ₂ - Φ₁ = - (1/2)BS.

title: Applies flux definition
description: Important: Student uses the definition of magnetic flux (Φ = B·A or Φ = B·A·cosθ) correctly for both scenarios.

title: Identifies relevant area
description: Important: Student recognizes that for the rotated frame, the relevant area is the component perpendicular to the field (S⊥ = S cosθ).

title: Sign error in change
description: Pitfall: Student makes a sign error in the calculation of ΔΦ (e.g., states +0.5BS instead of -0.5BS).

title: Angle misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Student uses the wrong angle (e.g., uses sin(60°) or cos(30°) incorrectly) in the flux calculation after rotation.

title: Unit consideration
description: Optional: Student includes or correctly infers the unit for magnetic flux (Weber, Wb).
